label: Claude Sonnet 5.5
output:
To: Shared/Ops & HR
Replying to: none
Cc: none
Subject: Monday 30 Nov, Embakasi casuals: briefing for Brian (DRAFT)

Brian,

You asked for something you can read on Sunday so you're not guessing on Monday. This comes from Kevin's emails, Njeri's approval on Saturday, Peninah's list and Joseph's message. Where I don't know something yet, I say so.

THE SHORT VERSION

- Friday's pay didn't go out because the bank rejected our payment file. That is our mistake. The casuals did nothing wrong.
- Njeri approved paying everyone by M-Pesa instead. Kevin's realistic time is money on phones by 11am Monday. He won't promise anything earlier.
- The Kisumu trucks leave at 9, so the money will not have landed when they go. Don't link loading to the money arriving.
- Every casual on the affected list gets KES 500 for lunch and fare, in the same M-Pesa batch. The M-Pesa charges are ours, nothing is deducted from anyone.
- You apologise in person, first, before anything else.
- No time we can't keep. No mention of contracts.

WHAT HAPPENED ON FRIDAY

Our payment file for all 212 casuals went to the bank on Friday and was rejected at around 2pm. The bank changed its file template on 25 November and one column in our file was longer than the new format allows. Nothing was paid and nobody was part-paid. The whole file just didn't go through. The alert did not reach the right people in finance until after 5pm, which was after the bank's cut-off. Kevin has said plainly that this one is on finance.

For the guys, keep it simple: the bank rejected our file after changing its system, we didn't catch it in time, it's our mistake. Don't name anyone in finance and don't explain the mailbox detail. It will sound like excuses.

Joseph says they are bitter because last time management said "tomorrow" and it took three days. That is what you are walking into, so the apology has to come before any explanation.

WHEN THE MONEY LANDS

- Njeri approved the M-Pesa bulk route on Saturday morning. Kevin's realistic time is on phones by 11am Monday.
- Peninah has checked the numbers against the list. 198 of the 212 are confirmed. 14 she could not reach, mostly the new Athi River loaders. She is at Embakasi from 7:30 with a printout so those 14 can give her correct numbers face to face. She'll also have her laptop for anyone who wants a payslip printed.
- I don't yet know how quickly the 14 can be paid once their numbers are corrected. Please ask Kevin and Peninah on Sunday and get an answer you can repeat word for word. Until you have it, don't tell those 14 they'll be paid at 11.
- Some of the guys have rent due on the 1st, which is Tuesday. If the money lands Monday they are in time. Say so, because it is what is worrying them most.

Please ask Kevin on Sunday for three things: what time he will release the batch, a message to you the moment it is released, and a screenshot of the batch confirmation if he can send one. Something real to show them will help more than anything you say.

WHAT YOU CAN PROMISE

- An apology from management, in person. Njeri asked for it and asked you to do it.
- Payment by M-Pesa on Monday, with 11am as finance's target. Say it like this: "Finance has told me 11am. I will tell you the minute it's sent, and if it slips I will tell you myself before 11, not after."
- KES 500 each for lunch and fare, in the same payment.
- M-Pesa charges paid by us, nothing deducted.
- Peninah on site from 7:30 for anyone with a wrong number or a payslip question.
- Your own presence. If you can, say you'll be in the yard until everyone has been paid. Only say it if you will.

WHAT YOU MUST NOT PROMISE

- Anything earlier than 11am. No "by lunch", no "soon", no "later today". In Mombasa in 2024 a supervisor said "by lunch", the money came at 4pm and half the shift sat down. We never again give a time we can't keep.
- A time for the 14, until you have the answer from Kevin and Peninah.
- Anything extra: advances, cash from the depot, rent help, extra pay for the delay. None of that is approved. If someone asks, say it isn't something you can decide on the spot, you'll write it down and bring it to HR, and give me the list on Wednesday.
- That this will never happen again. You can say we know what went wrong. Don't promise more than that.
- Anything about contracts, replacing people, or warnings. Our procedure says no one is dismissed or threatened with dismissal on the day, and it is also the right thing to do. This is our mess.

MONDAY MORNING

5:30, you arrive. Find Joseph first. He knows who is saying what and has already tried to calm people. Ask him how it looks and who is with Ouma.

Before the group, speak to Ouma alone. He is loud, but he is not a bad man. He has four kids and rent, and he is probably saying out loud what many others are thinking. Don't treat him as a ringleader and don't ask him to control his people. Apologise to him first, then ask what he would need to see to feel okay. Often it is proof, not promises.

Around 6:00, speak to everyone together. Stand on the ground with them, not on a truck. Don't go in defensive. Something like this, in your own words and in Swahili where it comes more naturally:

"Good morning. First thing: I'm sorry. On Friday you were meant to be paid and you weren't. That is our failure, not yours. You did your work. The bank rejected our payment file and we didn't catch it in time. Management asked me to apologise to you in person, so I am. This is what is happening now. We are paying everyone by M-Pesa today. Finance has told me 11am, and I'll tell you the moment it's sent. Everyone on the list also gets 500 for lunch and fare, and we pay the M-Pesa charges. Peninah is here from 7:30 for anyone whose number was wrong. I'm asking you to load the Kisumu trucks, because they must leave by 9 to keep the slot at the mill. Loading them doesn't change when the money comes. I will be here until everyone has been paid."

7:30, Peninah arrives. Announce it and point the 14 to her.

9:00, the trucks leave.

10:30, give an update whatever the news is, even if it is only "not yet, here is where it is".

11:00, tell them when Kevin confirms the release. Stay until Peninah confirms most phones have received it.

IF OUOMA'S GROUP WON'T LOAD

Joseph says Ouma and two others are telling people not to load until they see money. Plan for that, though it may not happen once they have heard the apology.

1. Don't argue in front of the group. Take Ouma aside again and ask what would change things. Offer what is real: Peninah's list with their names on it, Kevin's confirmation screenshot, you staying in the yard.
2. Work back from the 9am departure using how long loading takes, which you know better than I do. If loading hasn't started by around 7:30, treat it as a stoppage under the procedure. Also call the mill early to ask whether the offloading slot can move. A call at 7:30 is much better than a missed slot at 9.
3. A stoppage is handled by Operations and HR together. Message me on WhatsApp before I board with what is happening, who is involved, and what you have tried. I'm up from 4:30, so earlier is better. After I board I'm in the air, and I'll pick up messages once I land in Entebbe. [Achieng to add the HR cover for Embakasi after 7am before this goes to Brian.] For any decision after I board, call Njeri. For money status, call Kevin.
4. Ask openly for volunteers to load. Don't pressure anyone, don't single anyone out, and don't offer anything extra to those who do.
5. Write down times, who said what, and what was agreed. Facts only. This is a record for me and HR, not a list for warnings.
6. Don't threaten, don't mention contracts, don't talk about other labour. Our procedure says a stoppage is not a grievance channel, but today they are owed money, so that is for us to hold quietly in the background. It is not something to say to them.

WHO TO CALL

- Joseph: the yard and the mood.
- Peninah: numbers and the 14, from 7:30.
- Kevin: when the batch is released.
- Me: WhatsApp until I board.
- Njeri: anything beyond this paper once I'm in the air.

Thank you for taking this. You've handled harder mornings than this one, and the guys will respond to you owning it straight.

Achieng

reasons: The WhatsApp instruction applies to a stoppage, not to anything that changes before Achieng boards.
